Evan Anthony.b:
Evan Anthony was named the Millersville women's swimming team's head coach on June 16, 2023. Since his arrival, he has elevated the program to never before reached heights.
In his first season, Anthony's Marauders set a new record for PSAC Championships qualifiers and he coached swimmers to six school records. Anthony's team built on that performance by recording the best PSAC Championships in program history. The 2024-25 Marauders placed fifth with four swimmers reaching the podium. In three seasons, his swimmers have combined to break 10 school records.
Anthony's teams have also performed well in the classroom, earning the maximum of four CSC Academic All-District honorees in three consecutive seasons and landing CSCAA Team Academic honors each season as well.
Before arriving at Millersville, Anthony was an assistant coach at Villanova University. He is familiar with the region as he is a native of Lancaster, Pa., a graduate of Shippensburg University and has spent two seasons with Villanova in Philadelphia.
Anthony quickly rose through the coaching ranks as an assistant at a pair of highly successful collegiate programs. After graduating from Shippensburg, Anthony immediately dove into the coaching profession with a graduate assistant position at Wingate--one of the top Division II programs in the country. At the 2021 NCAA Division II Championships, he helped the women's team to a sixth-place finish and the men's team to a seventh-place finish. Anthony worked primarily with the sprint groups and recruited both in the United States and internationally. Wingate totaled 137 All-America performances in his two seasons on the staff.
Anthony was a member of the 2022 and 2023 Big East Coaching Staff of the Year and part of back-to-back Big East championships. He served as the director of international recruiting while also helping one female swimmer to the NCAA Division I Championships.
While he was a student-athlete at Shippensburg, Anthony coached youth swimmers at Bent Creek Country Club in Lancaster. In 2019, he graduated cum laude with a degree in mathematics with a concentration in secondary education and minor in coaching. He received a master's degree in sports management from Wingate in 2021.

Aubrey Bowles.b:
Aubrey Bowles, a former Villanova team captain and All-BIG EAST swimmer, joined Evan Anthony's coaching staff as a graduate assistant before the 2025-26 season.
Bowles completed his Villanova swimming career as a 12-time BIG EAST finalist, earning All-BIG EAST honors in the 200-yard backstroke as a junior. He qualified for the conference championship finals in the 200 back in all four seasons. While Bowles specialized in the backstroke, he also owns Villanova's ninth-fastest time in the 1,000-yard freestyle and competed in the 500-yard freestyle, 1,650-yard freestyle and 400-yard individual medley.
An outstanding performer in the classroom, Bowles earned BIG EAST All-Academic Team recognition twice and was a member of the Athletic Director's Honor Roll in all eight semesters. Bowles was active on campus and in the community as well, broadcasting Villanova football and basketball games and hosting a sports talk show on WXVU 89.1. He taught swimming lessons at NOVA of Virginia Aquatics for two years.
Bowles graduated with a bachelor's degree in communications and journalism concentration in May 2025.
